system.name: UNIKIE-BENCH
system.one_liner: A unified benchmark for evaluating large multimodal models on key information extraction from document images, in constrained-category and open-category tracks.

content.variant_note: a task-formulation panel plus two track panels, each a nested taxonomy of domains and scenarios with real document thumbnails and counts under the title
content.argues: UNIKIE-BENCH poses key information extraction as schema-guided structured prediction and covers it with two complementary tracks that span many document domains, types, scenarios and languages.
content.subject: A schema plus a document image going through an LMM into a filled JSON, and the document domains and types of the two tracks as thumbnails.

lessons.what_to_learn: Open a benchmark overview with one panel that defines the task through an empty and a filled structured output around a model icon, then show each track as a nested taxonomy: titled boxes with rows of real thumbnails under short labels and a count line under the panel title.
lessons.suits: Benchmarks and datasets whose coverage is best shown by real samples per category, plus a short task definition with structured output.

evidence: UNIKIE-BENCH is built upon a schema-guided KIE formulation to enable end-to-end evaluation of LMMs.
It comprises two complementary evaluation tracks: the constrained-category KIE track and the open-category KIE track.

summary: UNIKIE-BENCH is a benchmark for key information extraction (KIE) from document images by large multimodal models. Figure 1 has three rounded panels. The left one defines the task: an empty JSON schema and an invoice image go into a robot-head icon labelled Large Multimodal Model, and a filled JSON comes out. The middle panel, the constrained-category track (4,472 documents, 3 domains, 11 scenarios), and the right panel, the open-category track (1,661 documents, 4 types, 2 languages), are drawn as stacked boxes with navy title bands and rows of real document thumbnails under short scenario or type labels. The palette is nearly monochrome navy on white, with serif titles and monospace code.
